content: Before taking mifepristone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies to this medication or other substances. Mifepristone may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication can slow the elimination of other drugs from your body, potentially altering their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications may affect how mifepristone is removed from your body, impacting its efficacy. Mifepristone may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss alternative, non-hormonal birth control options with your doctor or pharmacist while using this medication. Beta-blocker medications, such as metoprolol, propranolol, or glaucoma eye drops like timolol, may mask symptoms of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), such as a rapid or pounding heartbeat. Many drugs can influence blood sugar levels, making it more challenging to manage. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist to understand how it may affect your blood sugar. Regularly monitor your blood sugar as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high or low blood sugar. Mifepristone may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcohol consumption. This medication may also cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can be exacerbated by certain medical conditions or medications. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood, often caused by diuretics, severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting, may increase the risk of QT prolongation. Inform your doctor if you have any of these conditions. Mifepristone must not be used during pregnancy, as it can result in pregnancy loss. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. This medication can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as unconsciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
